examples.problem: Find the integral of $\dfrac 1 {2x} + 3x$ with respect to $x.$
examples.worked_solution:
Applying the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{1}{2x}+3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{2x}\,\text{d}x+\int 3x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+3\int x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}ln⁡|x|+3\cdot \frac{{x}^{1+1}}{1+1}+C \\  & =\frac{ln⁡|x|}{2}+\frac{3{x}^{2}}{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we apply the constant factor rule and take the coefficient $-\frac{2}{5}$ out of the integral. Then we compute the integral of $\frac{1}{x},$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int -\frac{2}{5x}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{2}{5}\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{2}{5}ln⁡|x|+C.\end{aligned}
$$
